q: An astigmatic eye in which one focal line lies on the retina and the other lies in front of it has:
w: Simple myopic astigmatism places one focal line on the retina and the other in front, so a minus cylinder alone corrects it. Compound myopic astigmatism puts both lines in front of the retina.
k: One line on retina, one in front = simple myopic astigmatism.

q: When one focal line falls in front of the retina and the other falls behind it, the astigmatism is:
w: Mixed astigmatism straddles the retina: one focal line in front and one behind. It is corrected with a combined plus and minus cylinder (a spherocylinder that crosses zero).
k: One line in front, one behind = mixed astigmatism.

q: A myopic eye whose refracting surfaces are too strong while its axial length is normal has:
w: Refractive myopia comes from over-powerful refracting surfaces in an eye of normal length, whether from steep curvature or a high lens index. Axial myopia instead comes from an eye that is too long.
k: Normal length but too-strong surfaces = refractive myopia.
